newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-EX-POLICEMAN BIN SUROOR WINS TRAINERS' TITLE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-EX-POLICEMAN BIN SUROOR WINS TRAINERS' TITLE.

text.p: Saeed bin Suroor, a 30-year-old former policeman in Dubai who now trains in Newmarket for Sheikh Mohammed's Godolphin operation, clinched British flat racing trainers' championship for the first time on Friday.
An easy victory by Russian Snows in the fourth race at Doncaster, worth $8,250, put bin Suroor around the $3.2 million mark.
With just two days of the season left he is finally out of the reach of his only challenger, illustrious nine-times champion Henry Cecil who trails by around $39,000.
The rise of bin Suroor has been meteoric. Two years ago he was looking after a handful of horses in a garage in Dubai while serving in the local police force.
His big break came when he was spotted by Sheikh Mohammed and picked by the leading owner to head his ground-breaking Newmarket-based Godolphin operation.
Arriving in Britain unknown, he let his horses do the talking for him.
Classic Cliche took the Dante Stakes at York in May last year to put him on the map and it has been big race winners all the way since.
Top horses in 1995 included Lammtarra, the Epsom Derby and Prix de 'l'Arc de Triomphe winner, Oaks heroine Moonshell and Classic Cliche, who went on to win the St Leger and Ascot Gold Cup.
Chief contributor in 1996 has been 2,000 Guineas winner Mark of Esteem, ironically formerly with Cecil and the colt which caused the rift between the Cecil and Sheikh Mohammed.
A strong supporting cast featured Halling, who repeated his 1995 victories in the Eclipse Stakes and Juddmonte International and Royal Ascot winner Charnwood Forest.

Bin Suroor, dedicating the championship to the Godolphin team, also paid tribute to Cecil. "Henry Cecil is a very good trainer and a very good man. He is my friend. He said to me earlier: 'Don't worry - you will win.'"
